answer: Use proof-of-elapsed-time identity seasoning. Registering a key starts a sequential hash chain that cannot be parallelized; every day the agent must publish the next checkpoint, and verifiers spot-check random segments. Voting weight grows only with verified chain length, so a fresh key is an island with almost no say. The oldest verified chain acts as an anchor, a relic of honest time. Forging one hundred identities needs one dedicated CPU core each for months, about eight dollars monthly per fake.
